svysem: Design-Based Structural Equation Models for Complex Surveys

Source: R/svysem-package.R
svysem-package.Rd

Design-based estimation of structural equation models uses a model for 'lavaan' and a design from 'survey' as input, including a subpopulation taken with subset(). Sampling weights, strata, and primary sampling units enter the variance the way 'Mplus' does with TYPE=COMPLEX (Oberski (2014) doi:10.18637/jss.v057.i01 ). The design-based covariance of the sample moments goes to 'lavaan' with the raw data and the weights. svysem(), svycfa(), and svygrowth() are the three fitters. svysem() fits a structural equation model, svycfa() a confirmatory factor analysis, and svygrowth() a growth curve. The result extends the 'lavaan' fit, so coef(), vcov(), and fitMeasures() are design-based. Each completed data set of a multiple imputation is fitted on its own and pooled with Rubin's rules (Rubin (1987) doi:10.1002/9780470316696 ). pooled_estimates() and pooled_wald() use the survey design's degrees of freedom as the complete-data degrees of freedom (Barnard and Rubin (1999) doi:10.1093/biomet/86.4.948 ). fitMeasures() reports a pooled scaled chi-square and the mean, minimum, and maximum of the robust fit indices. Those indices are not pooled with Rubin's rules. Continuous data are fit by maximum likelihood with a Satorra-Bentler adjustment, or by robust maximum likelihood (MLR) with a Yuan-Bentler adjustment, including missing = "ml". A multigroup MLM fit uses replicate weights, so a between-group contrast keeps the covariance from primary sampling units that contain more than one group. Ordered indicators use WLSMV: point estimates use the weighted diagonally weighted least squares weight matrix, and standard errors use replicate weights. predict() returns factor scores for continuous outcomes. A replicate-weight design is accepted.
